claim: Observe actual heterogeneous CPU topology and validate a reversible resource policy for background Agent work without restricting the desktop to little cores.
oracle: Eight online CPUs and DT/frequency-policy groups are read from the phone; transient workload cgroup enforces requested CPUWeight/CPUQuota/Nice and cleans up on exit. No physical responsiveness claim until a loaded touch journey passes.

user_journey.scenario: Open Files and type while API Agents wait/run tools; interrupt/reconnect or manually adjust settings, then recover the desktop.
user_journey.expected: Desktop remains responsive and Agent processes retain progress; remote test alone cannot accept physical feel.

invariants: Observe cpu_capacity, compatible and cpufreq policy before choosing limits
Retain Linux scheduler access to all online cores for UI
Only task-owned transient background cgroup; no global affinity or IRQ writes
No sustained load while thermal telemetry unavailable
gitnexus: Not applicable: standalone phone experiment outside neweval execution graph; inspect systemd command and actual cgroup files instead

unit.red: Reject nonpositive or excessive quota/weight and malformed CPU selection if a configurable launcher is introduced
unit.green: Not applicable to read-only topology inventory; policy helper validation required before reusable launcher

limitations: No thermal zones in prior inventory; avoid extended stress
CPU distribution cannot repair missing GPU, modem, WiFi or camera drivers
Node main event loop is single threaded; worker processes/threads and Go scheduler require workload-specific configuration
No background Harness production workload yet
exit_gate: Record measured topology; implement policy only after defining bounded load and recovery checks; promote default settings only after independent load test and physical journey.
